LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 11.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 11 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to listen carefully? 2. How can we become better listeners?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to oral presentations (dialogues or poems on topical issues) containing words with the sound /aɪ/,

2. identify words with the sound /aɪ/ from texts,

3. practise saying selected tongue twisters collaboratively, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to oral presentations (dialogues or poems on topical issues) containing words with the sound /aɪ/,
2. identify words with the sound /aɪ/ from texts,
3. practise saying selected tongue twisters collaboratively, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner makes short speeches while collaborating with peers.

• Self-Efficacy is developed as the learner picks out the target sounds from poems or stories.

Values:
Love is enhanced as the learner prepares and makes speeches with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education (Effective listening) is cultivated when the learner listens to their peers say tongue-twisters and

make short speeches.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies fluency in listening and nonverbal skills in learning similar concepts in Kiswahili.
